text:
mel: heads-up — saw a cluster of OOMs on gpu-quiet5 around 03:20 UTC immediately after today's kernel selection change. prefcache memory shot up and we fell back to the tiny-model variant for ~2m.

sasha: ugh. any repro on canary? which kernel variant rolled?

mel: rolled kernel v3.4.2 (attention-optim1) -> it changed the workspace allocation policy (more eager slab growth). repro on canary when load > 600 qps.

arjun: paste of the most relevant logs:
```
[03:20:11] runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[03:20:11] runtime: attempted alloc 134217728 bytes for workspace
[03:20:12] prefcache: shard-7 used 512MB -> 1.8GB after prefetch batch
[03:20:12] kernel: selected attention-optim1, batch_size=32, sequence=1024
[03:20:13] fallback: routed to tiny-model v0.9
```

arjun: quick metric snapshot from the interval:
- prefcache global hit-rate: 0.62 (dropped from 0.87 pre-roll)
- active shards: 24 -> 36
- prefetched keys per-request avg: 48 -> 120
- mean workspace per-kernel: 450MB -> 1.1GB

dave: that workspace jump looks like the kernel now reserves full workspace for worst-case sequence instead of lazy growth. did we switch kernel-level workspace_size_hint semantics?

mel: yes — kernel team toggled 'prealloc_workspace=true' to reduce jitter under micro-batching; inadvertently raced with prefcache prefetch that doubled KV footprints.

ruo: two orthogonal issues: (1) kernel prealloc growth, (2) prefetch throttle. Prefetch is currently unconstrained per-shard when eviction pressure < threshold. When prealloc happens, combined demand crosses OOM.

katie: any quick mitigations we can flip?

mel: short list: 
- flip prealloc off (revert flag) on the rollout.
- apply soft cap to per-shard prefetch (slice and backoff) e.g. max_prefetch_inflight = 48 keys.
- reduce kernel workspace hint when sequence > 512 to use progressive growth.

arjun: tried a static patch locally: set max_prefetch_inflight=48 and progressive workspace policy. ran synthetic replay at 800 qps for 10m: no OOMs, hit-rate settles ~0.74, tail latency +30ms but no fallbacks.

sasha: can we do a smarter handoff: when kernel prealloc is enabled AND shard footprint > X, throttle prefetch or trigger a graceful eviction sweep?

dave: propose policy: prefetch_handoff_threshold = 0.7 of gpu_free_mem. If predicted prefetch + kernel_prealloc > threshold -> demote prefetch to 'deferred' and mark keys with soft-ttl to be rehydrated lazily. Also emit a metric prefcache.prefetch.demoted_by_handoff.

ruo: +1. need to be careful with race while computing predicted prefetch: use moving average of recent prefetch inflight sizes and add kernel_hint for currently scheduled kernels.

mel: small config we piloted in canary: 
```
prefetch:
  max_inflight_per_shard: 48
  handoff_threshold_fraction: 0.68
  demotion_mode: soft-ttl
kernel:
  workspace_policy: progressive
  prealloc_workspace: false
```

mel: results on canary (30m): 
- OOMs: 4 -> 0
- prefcache hit-rate: 0.62 -> 0.71
- avg tail latency (p99 gen): +18ms
- throughput unchanged

katie: that's promising. team wants SLO-preserving grad roll? what's the rollback plan?

arjun: rollback is just flip prealloc true back and raise max_inflight_per_shard. We should also add a short-circuit circuit breaker: if fallback rate > 0.5% for 2m -> auto-revert.

sasha: two follow-ups for longer-term: (1) smarter shard-sizing: shrink hot shards into micro-shards to reduce single-shard prefetch spikes, (2) kv-entry compression for prefetched blobs to reduce peak memory.

dave: micro-shard idea is tricky for consistency but could reduce OOM blast radius. we should simulate hit-rate vs mem cost for 2->4x shard split.

ruo: i ran a quick sim with 10M requests sampling; results: 
- splitting hot shards 2x reduces max single-shard footprint by ~45% but increases cross-shard traffic by ~12% (marginal hit-rate loss ~0.03).

mel: tl;dr: immediate mitigation = revert kernel prealloc + prefetch caps + progressive workspace. mid-term: shard-splitting simulation + compression. Deployment plan: rollback flag on next host-level canary (in 15m), apply prefetch cap rollout to all canaries, monitor prefcache.prefetch.demoted_by_handoff, fallback.rate, and p99 gen.

deploy-bot: deploy started for kernel prealloc rollback on cluster gpu-quiet5-canary-1 (id: deploy-3492).

katie: assign owners: mel (rollback and monitoring dashboards), arjun (prefetch cap rollout), dave (shard-splitting simulation), ruo (compression PoC).

mel: noted. will post follow-up with metric dashboards and repro snippets. thanks all :thumbsup:

sasha: thanks — nice quick triage.
